relevance_note: The paper describes four individuals with TNFAIP3 variants: 'Four HA20 patients in the two families presented with childhood-onset recurrent oral and genital ulcers'.
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON from my reading and transcribed Table 1 (patients as columns; column headers 'Patient 1'..'Patient 4' under row 'Patient'), checked against the table. Table 1 '–' cells are not defined as absent in the legend, so they are treated as not reported; '+' read as present. Exclusions come only from text ('did not show any ophthalmological...'). Table 1 'Age at diagnosis' corresponds to the BD diagnosis in the text. Labels: pedigree labels III-1 and II-2 occur in both families, so family 1 relatives are 'III-1 (Family 1)' and 'II-2 (Family 1)'; Patient 3 is III-1 and Patient 4 is II-2 of Fig. 1b. 'parent of Patient 3' is the parent other than Patient 4 (WES was performed on both parents); the paper gives no result or features for this person. Unaffected, untested relatives (family 1 mother II-6; family 2 I-1, I-2, II-3, II-4: 'no BD-like symptoms') were left out as neither tested nor affected. Relatives III-1, II-5 and II-2 of family 1 are affected but their TNFAIP3 status is not reported, so they have no variant rows. The family 2 deletion also includes PERP; no separate PERP variant row. ref [8] patient (13 Mb deletion, from the Discussion) is included under the v4 rule; the 50 previously reported cases in Table 2/S1/S2 are group-level only, and DECIPHER/DGV/ExAC deletion carriers are database entries without individual clinical detail, so no rows. Normal investigations recorded as written: colonoscopy without abnormality (Patient 3 at 5 years, Patient 4 at 18 years), which exclude nothing more specific; Patient 3 later had intestinal ulcers on endoscopy. Patient 4: Table 1 Fever cell is '–' but the text says she 'presented fever with tonsillitis and lymphadenitis several times a year ... not apparently periodic'; recorded recurrent fever as observed from the text, flagged as uncertain. Patient 1: table lists genital ulcers '+' while the text mentions oral and perianal ulcers; both recorded. Abstract counts ('three of four patients' with fever, 'two of the four' digestive ulcers) were not used to exclude anyone. Heterozygosity for c.1434C>A from the Introduction sentence naming the single novel heterozygous variant; zygosity of the deletion not stated. No contradictions found beyond the Patient 4 fever cell.
